beliefs.practice: Create a single Motor client (MotorClient) at app startup and reuse it everywhere (do not create a new client per request); close it on shutdown.

Read the cluster connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) or from Azure Key Vault / managed identity at runtime; never commit credentials into the repository or logs and provide a .env.example with a placeholder.
Configure the Motor client with TLS enabled and sensible connection-pool settings (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize) appropriate for the orchestrator's concurrency, and reuse the pool across async tasks.

Use short, idempotent transactions: perform each orchestrator step and the atomic update in a single MongoDB multi-document transaction via Motor sessions/with_transaction, keep transactions short, and avoid user interaction while a transaction is open.

Protect concurrent state updates with optimistic concurrency: include a version or lastUpdated timestamp in the query predicate (e.g., findOneAndUpdate where version = X -> version = X+1) so a competing updater fails rather than silently overwriting.

Model the application as a single document with an embedded history array only if the history is bounded; otherwise store transitions in a separate history collection to avoid unbounded array growth and document size limits (MongoDB 16MB limit).

Create a unique index on the application identifier (e.g., { application_id: 1 }) and create a compound index for the orchestrator's main lookup patterns (e.g., { state: 1, priority: -1 } or { state: 1, next_run_at: 1 }).

Add a partial or sparse index on fields only present for active applications (e.g., partialFilterExpression: { state: 'PENDING' }) to speed selection of next work item and reduce RU/cost for index maintenance.

When storing vectors, use a dedicated field with a consistent floating-point format (float32 array) and create the vector index with explicit parameters: dimension, indexType (HNSW), M/efConstruction or similar, and metric (cosine/dot/ivf inner product) suitable for your similarity needs.

When performing vector + metadata filtering, push the metadata filters into the same query so the engine can apply prefilters before the vector search; project away the large vector field when only metadata is required (use projection to exclude vector field).

Use exponential backoff and retry logic for transient errors and rate-limited responses (HTTP 429 for Cosmos DB or equivalent Mongo error codes), limit total retry time, and apply idempotency safeguards for operations retried after partial failure.
Keep transactions and updates small (touch only the fields you need); avoid updating large vector blobs inside a transaction to reduce RU consumption and avoid timeouts.

Use projection in queries to avoid transferring vectors or other large fields unless required (e.g., collection.find({state:'READY'},{vector:0}) ), and use batch sizes / pagination for loops scanning many docs.

When using Beanie with Motor, initialize Beanie once (init_beanie) with the Motor client and document models at startup; reuse the same Motor client for Beanie operations and pass session objects into Beanie/Motor calls when performing transactions.

Record audited state transitions in the document (actor, timestamp, previous_state, next_state, metadata) and make this append operation part of the same atomic update or transaction so the document never loses the transition record.

Avoid long-lived change streams or tailable cursors for orchestration unless you validate the Mongo compatibility and performance for the managed service; instead use polling/cron with indexed queries for next work item selection.
Provision indexes before bulk-loading or running large backfills; creating vector indexes can be expensive—create them once and then load data to avoid repeated reindex cost.

Limit the size of embedded history array writes with $push + $slice or use capped history length (e.g., $push: { history: { $each:[entry], $position:0, $slice:100 } }) to prevent unbounded growth inside the document.
Design unit tests to mock the DB and Motor sessions for fast CI runs; separate integration tests that actually seed and mutate the live cluster and run those only when explicitly allowed.
Monitor RU/throughput and slow query plans using the provider's tools; add indexes for slow filters/sorts (use explain() in the documentdb MCP tools) and set alerts for RU throttling (429s).

When using transactions, implement retry-on-transient-failure logic recommended for MongoDB transactions (retry the entire with_transaction callable when encountering transient errors or UnknownTransactionCommitResult), and ensure idempotency of the transaction body.

Keep per-document size under MongoDB limits by avoiding storing large file blobs or high-dimension vectors inline if they will push document size up; consider external object storage (Blob) for large payloads with references in documents.
